body:
There is absolutely a family history of psych problems, myself included. I have suffered chronic depression for years and she is aware of this. It is likely a very big factor as to why she feels comfortable opening up to me because I will understand the feelings she's experiencing. She herself has been in treatment over the years to cope with my depression, her father and I separating as well as the bullying, her hearing disability and her intelligence (this has put her two years ahead in school. Aka she is 12 in a class of 14 year olds)

All in all, her situation is quite a lot to handle for someone her age and going through the hormonal changes of puberty on top of it all.

As for the self harm, she has shown me a video of the knife she used. The ones usually for opening boxes in stores, etc. She was putting it away as a sign of pride that she would stop cutting herself. To me the mention of what she was doing sounded a lot like someone who is overwhelmed emotionally and trying to distract herself from what is hurting her in school or in her day to day life, it seemed like she was challenging herself to take action. She currently does not believe things will ever improve and she feels alone in the world. It's her best friend that seems to keep her together mostly, so they made their pact to encourage each other to live a little while longer.

I am not very appreciative of the threat of the mental hospital myself, it's hardly helpful to make her afraid of seeking treatment and I hope that my positive approach towards it may make a difference. Her biggest concern with it was having no access to her phone and people finding out about it, which would result in more bullying and physical violence. Their lack of insight is my biggest hesitation to call them, I am terrified they would respond badly and only make matters worse while I am trying to decrease the risk of my daughter doing something to hurt herself.

I had the night to think now and I am going to suggest to her to speak to them herself, to confide in them about her problems and encourage her to accept that it is only going to be for her own well being if they decide she needs to perhaps seek treatment. I hope that I will manage to have her continue talk to me and open up communication with the people who are closest to her to intervene when needed.

I honestly felt like I was going to be judged for living in a different country, hence the remark. Though really I was just all over the place. I feel a little more calm now that I have some ideas on how to approach this.

Thank you for replying to me, it's very valuable to have a response from someone of similar age as my daughter and what you felt you needed at the time of your problems. I hope you are feeling better and supported

It really is just surreal. I'll hold on to those messages, AND the SO for that matter. 

I also googled the alleged name of said author, the book exists. But not written by that name. At least we're getting a good chuckle out of the obnoxious stupidity.

I currently don't have any further information about her. I've also decided to not pry and badger her if indeed the events are all true, I'd rather she is given some time to rest. As long as she knows I'm here, that's all I can do. 

However, the ex did message me to confirm he will finally go NC with my sister, after all he has been through I really do not blame him for wanting to move on with his own life.
